questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Location and Extent of India' refers to.
questions.a: India lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere, extending roughly from 8°4'N to 37°6'N latitude and 68°7'E to 97°25'E longitude, covering about 3.28 million square kilometres.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Location and Extent of India'.
questions.a: India's latitudinal and longitudinal extent determines its position in South Asia and its size relative to other countries.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Location and Extent of India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Location and Extent

concepts.title: The Himalayan Mountains and Major Peaks

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Himalayan Mountains and Major Peaks' refers to.
questions.a: The Himalayas are the young fold mountains in the north of India, divided into three parallel ranges - the Himadri (Greater Himalayas), the Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) and the Shivaliks (Outer Himalayas) - and contain major peaks such as Mount Everest (8,848 m) and Kanchenjunga (8,586 m); other ranges include the Karakoram, Aravallis, Vindhyas, Satpuras and the Eastern and Western Ghats.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Himalayan Mountains and Major Peaks'.
questions.a: The Himalayas and other mountain ranges act as natural barriers, influence climate and drainage, and are the source of major perennial rivers; their peaks form natural boundaries between regions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Himalayan Mountains and Major Peaks' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Physical Divisions - The Himalayas and Mountain Ranges

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Northern Plains' refers to.
questions.a: The Northern Plains are a vast fertile plain formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems, lying between the Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Northern Plains'.
questions.a: The alluvial soil and flat terrain of the Northern Plains make them highly suitable for agriculture and dense human settlement.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Northern Plains' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Physical Divisions - The Northern Plains

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Peninsular Plateau' refers to.
questions.a: The Peninsular Plateau is the oldest and most stable landmass of India, a tableland composed of old crystalline and igneous rocks, divided into the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Peninsular Plateau'.
questions.a: The Peninsular Plateau is rich in minerals and has a varied relief that influences river drainage and vegetation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Peninsular Plateau' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Physical Divisions - The Peninsular Plateau

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Coastal Plains' refers to.
questions.a: The Coastal Plains are narrow strips of land along the eastern and western shores of India, divided into the Eastern Coastal Plain and the Western Coastal Plain.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Coastal Plains'.
questions.a: The coastal plains support fishing, agriculture and trade, and feature important deltas and lagoons.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Coastal Plains' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Physical Divisions - The Coastal Plains

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Indian Desert' refers to.
questions.a: The Indian Desert, also called the Thar Desert, is a dry, sandy and rocky region in western Rajasthan, characterised by very low rainfall and extreme temperature variation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Indian Desert'.
questions.a: The Thar Desert's arid climate results from the monsoon winds losing moisture before reaching western Rajasthan.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Indian Desert' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Physical Divisions - The Desert

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Islands' refers to.
questions.a: India has two groups of islands: the Lakshadweep Islands in the Arabian Sea (coral islands) and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal (volcanic and mountainous islands).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Islands'.
questions.a: The islands differ in origin and location, supporting unique ecosystems and biodiversity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Islands' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Physical Divisions - The Islands

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rivers of India' refers to.
questions.a: Indian rivers are classified into Himalayan rivers (perennial, fed by snow and rainfall) and Peninsular rivers (seasonal, rain-fed), which form fertile valleys and support agriculture.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rivers of India'.
questions.a: Himalayan rivers are perennial and form large deltas, while Peninsular rivers are seasonal and flow in rift valleys.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rivers of India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Rivers of India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Climate Variation Across Regions' refers to.
questions.a: India experiences a wide range of climates due to its vast size and varied relief, from the tropical climate of the south to the temperate and cold climate of the north and the arid climate of the desert.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Climate Variation Across Regions'.
questions.a: Latitude, altitude and distance from the sea together determine the regional climate variation across India.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Climate Variation Across Regions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Climate Variation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Natural Vegetation and Wildlife' refers to.
questions.a: Natural vegetation refers to plants that grow naturally without human aid; India has diverse vegetation types - tropical evergreen, tropical deciduous, thorn forests, mountain forests and mangrove forests - supporting rich wildlife.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Natural Vegetation and Wildlife'.
questions.a: The type of natural vegetation in a region is determined by temperature, rainfall and soil, and it in turn supports the wildlife of that region.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Natural Vegetation and Wildlife' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Natural Vegetation and Wildlife
